Emily — thanks for the clear ask. Short answer: yes on microburst allowances (configurable) and yes we can structure a short-term onboarding credit for committed pools.

High level:
- Microburst SLA: We offer a configurable burst window that can be purchased as part of the Dedicated commitment. Typical configs we sell: 5-minute burst with 3x baseline tokens, 15-minute burst with 1.5x baseline, and an enterprise option with 30-minute smoothing. Each tier maps to a per-token uplift.
- Credits: For a 12-month commit we can provide a 10% effective credit applied to months 1–3 as either a bill credit or as additional token allotment. For a 6-month commit we can offer a 7% credit.

I'll loop Marissa and Karthik for structure and concessions so we can confirm exact wording for procurement. Attaching the updated proposal with a sample microburst matrix.

Looping in a concise concession plan so procurement has clear options. My recommendation below (keep external recipients on thread so Emily sees language).

Proposed commercial language (two-line summary):
- 12-month Reserved Pool (H100-heavy configuration) — base throughput T, includes 2x 5-minute microburst windows per day at up to 4x baseline token/sec. Effective onboarding credit: 10% of committed spend applied across months 1–3 as invoice credit.
- 6-month Reserved Pool (mixed H100/A100) — base throughput 0.9T, includes 1x 5-minute microburst/day at up to 3x baseline. Effective onboarding credit: 7% as token allotment in month 1.

Tradeoffs and rationale (internal):
- H100-heavy pool gives highest perf/$ for low-latency chat workloads; larger memory variants reduce model-sharding overhead during bursts. Offering more burst capacity on H100 is higher margin but supports EdgeScale's latency needs.
- Mixed fleet (H100 + A100) helps control cost and gives a lower commitment exposure if they want shorter term.
- Credit as token allotment avoids cash accounting headaches for finance; invoice credit is preferred by some procurement teams who want line-item reduction.

Karthik — confirm that the burst matrix in the attached spreadsheet aligns with engineering's safe thresholds and whether we should cap burst incidents per day/week. I want to avoid an open-ended SLA.

-Marissa

Emily / team — engineering confirms the microburst matrix in sla-microburst-matrix.xlsx with the following binding points:

- 5-minute microburst: up to 4x baseline tokens per second, up to 6 incidents/day (incidents are defined as aggregated contiguous time segments >= 30s). Latency percentile SLO during burst: p95 < 280ms for H100 instances, p95 < 420ms for A100.
- 15-minute microburst: up to 1.5x baseline, capped at 3 incidents/week.
- Incident accounting: bursts are measured at the pool level; if two distinct models cause overlapping spikes they count as a single incident.

Operational notes:
- We will instrument the pool with a burst-meter and provide daily usage breakdowns in the Console. If EdgeScale exceeds the licensed incident caps repeatedly (3 months running), we will trigger a capacity review and propose a tiered uplift schedule.
- For the 12-month H100 configuration we can hold the 10% onboarding credit as an invoice credit. For 6-month mixed we will do a token allotment in month 1.

Emily — if that aligns, we'll send a short amendment text for procurement/legal to attach to the MSA.

Karthik Iyer
SVP, Product Partnerships | Redwood Inference
